# Go++

> Go++ is a Go-compatible language that adds application-level syntax and compiles to ordinary Go. Source files use the `.gpp` extension; the command-line tool is `gpp`.

Use the guides and examples below as the primary source for writing Go++ code. Go++ code can use Go packages and interoperate with Go code.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): project overview, installation, and command reference.
- [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md): create and run a Go++ project.
- [Language guide](docs/guide/language.md): syntax and language behavior.
- [Standard library guide](docs/guide/standard-library.md): Go++ library packages.
- [Tooling guide](docs/guide/tooling.md): formatting, import repair, tests, docs, and LSP.

## Working with a Go++ project

- Run `gpp doc --json <symbol>` to look up public API documentation.
- Run `gpp lsp` to use compiler-backed editor diagnostics and language features.
- Run `gpp fmt`, `gpp fiximports`, `gpp build`, and `gpp test` as appropriate for the project.

## Documentation notes

- Treat the guides, feature index, examples, and `gpp doc` output as descriptions of current behavior.
- The [specification index](docs/reference/specifications.md) links to detailed specifications. A specification may describe behavior that is still planned; check the feature index and implementation-facing guides before relying on it.
